description:
We are a team combining technology, Earth science, creativity, and music to make NASA’s Earth data more accessible. For the Earth Information Jukebox challenge, we are building an interactive experience that transforms NASA Earth data and visualizations into dynamic soundscapes. 

Our goal is simple: help people not only see how our planet changes, but hear it too.
summary:
Earth Information Jukebox is an accessibility or first Earth science platform that transforms real NASA and partner climate datasets into interactive sound. Instead of relying only on charts and graphs, the platform enables users to hear long term changes in Earth's systems through a custom "Earth Orchestra" sonification engine.

The project uses global temperature, atmospheric CO₂, Arctic sea ice, and sea level datasets to create a synchronized audio and visual experience. Each dataset is assigned a unique musical role , allowing users to hear how Earth's systems evolve and interact over time. The platform also includes live visualizations, transcript generation, voice narration, keyboard navigation, and WCAG-inspired accessibility features to support a wide range of users , including blind and low-vision audiences.

Earth Information Jukebox addresses the challenge by making complex Earth science data more understandable, engaging, and inclusive. By combining scientific accuracy, accessibility, and creative data sonification, the project helps transform environmental measurements into a human experience. Our goal is to help people not only see Earth's changing systems, but also hear and understand them in a completely new way.
details:
Project Details

Earth Information Jukebox is an accessibility-first Earth science platform that transforms real climate and environmental datasets into interactive soundscapes. Instead of only displaying charts and graphs, the project allows users to hear changes in Earth's systems through sonification while simultaneously exploring synchronized visualizations, transcripts, and scientific context.

The platform uses verified datasets from NASA, NOAA, NSIDC, and the NASA Sea Level Change Team, including Global Surface Temperature, Atmospheric CO₂ Concentration, Arctic Sea Ice Extent, and Global Sea Level Rise records. These datasets are converted into sound using a custom Earth Orchestra sonification engine.

Each Earth system is assigned a unique musical role:

  • Global Temperature → Lead Voice
  • Atmospheric CO₂ → Harmony Layer
  • Arctic Sea Ice → Crystal Texture Layer
  • Sea Level Rise → Deep Bass Foundation
  • Climate Acceleration → Dynamic Trend Layer

As users move through time, they can hear Earth's changing systems evolve together while viewing synchronized charts, a planetary data orb, waveform analysis, and live transcripts.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project is designed to make Earth science more accessible, engaging, and intuitive for a broader audience.

Key benefits include:

  • Improves accessibility for blind and low-vision users through sound and spoken narration.
  • Helps students and the general public understand long-term climate trends in a more intuitive way.
  • Creates a stronger emotional connection to Earth science data.
  • Provides an alternative method of scientific communication beyond traditional graphs and tables.
  • Demonstrates how multisensory experiences can increase engagement with climate education.

Our goal is to help people not only see Earth's changing systems, but also hear and experience them.

Tools and Technologies Used

Languages

  • HTML5
  • CSS3
  • JavaScript (ES6)

Web Technologies

  • Web Audio API
  • HTML Canvas API
  • Speech Synthesis API
  • Responsive Web Design

Data Sources

  • NASA GISS GISTEMP
  • NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory
  • NSIDC Arctic Sea Ice Index
  • NASA Sea Level Change Team

Design and Development

  • GitHub
  • GitHub Pages
  • PowerPoint
  • WCAG 2.1 Accessibility Principles

Creativity and Innovation

Rather than mapping scientific values directly to simple tones, Earth Information Jukebox introduces the concept of an Earth Orchestra, where multiple planetary systems interact simultaneously as components of a living soundscape.

This approach turns climate data into a multisensory experience that combines science, accessibility, education, and sound design. Users can hear warming temperatures, increasing atmospheric CO₂, shrinking Arctic sea ice, and rising sea levels as interconnected parts of the same planetary story.

Factors Considered During Development

Our team focused on several key priorities:

  • Scientific accuracy and trustworthy data sources.
  • Accessibility for users with different abilities.
  • Educational value for students and the public.
  • Intuitive user experience and navigation.
  • Performance on low-spec devices.
  • Real-time audio generation without external services.
  • Visual and auditory synchronization.
  • Scalability for future Earth science datasets.

Earth Information Jukebox demonstrates how science, technology, accessibility, and creativity can work together to transform complex Earth observations into a human experience that is easier to understand, remember, and share.
